subject: RM_SiltTrap_Modern

observed.facings.png: One south panel on a checker alpha background. A low fence-like barrier runs diagonally from upper left to lower right. It has four square dark-brown timber posts, two of them doubled up at the right end, with four to five horizontal dark timber boards between them. Grey steel collars with bolts sit at the top and foot of each post, flat grey steel caps on top, and stacked bolted steel plates at the board ends. A strip of brown mud with clods runs along the foot, with dark wet patches and small ripples around the post bases. There is no yellow/black striping and no bright red.
observed.south.png: The same picture at native size. The cut-out is clean, with transparency around the object and mud strip. Timber grain is painterly, there is a little green-dark staining on the lowest board, and the steel reads as dull galvanized grey with visible bolts. The top faces of caps and boards are visible and lighter. The silhouette fills most of the canvas.
observed.scale.png: The barrier on a brown ground beside a vanilla human. It is about as tall as the pawn's torso and about 1.5 pawn widths or more long. Dark timber with light caps and mud at the foot still read clearly.
observed.siblings.png: Reference row. Scrapper is rusty patched planks with rope-bound posts. Industrial is an ugly stained concrete wall with concrete posts. Futuristic is white panels with cyan light strips and rounded caps. All share the same post layout, diagonal run, mud strip and waterline.
observed.assembled_1.png: Four looks in a row beside a human at game scale. Modern is the dark timber and grey steel one, the same size and layout as the others, and clearly distinct from the orange-rust Scrapper, pale concrete Industrial and white-cyan Futuristic. Its boards are darker and lower contrast against the brown ground than the others, but the posts and caps read.
observed.assembled_2.png: The same row at smaller scale, with overlapping labels. Modern reads as a dark post-and-rail fence with light caps.
observed.assembled_3.png: The same row at about 32 px per cell, with overlapping labels. Modern reads as a dark fence with paler post caps. Board detail is mostly gone, but the shape is readable and distinct from the siblings.

CAMERA.seen: Viewed from above at an angle, with lit top faces on caps and top board plus a front band on posts. The diagonal run is the same three-quarter construction as all the family siblings, and the owner approved that family.

LAYERS.seen: There is nothing to connect. Within the picture and the offline rows, nearer posts overlap the boards and the mud sits under the post feet.

ROTATIONS.seen: Graphic_Single: one picture serves every rotation, so nothing can disagree.

SIGNATURE.seen: Dark timber boards, square posts, galvanized steel brackets and caps, with mud and waterline at the foot, all as described.

MATERIAL.seen: Timber shows grain and stain variation. Steel shows dull grey with bolts and edge highlights. Neither reads as a coat of paint, and there is no tier-marker colour.

FOOTPRINT.seen: Measured visible height is 190 px, and the object fills the canvas without cropping. It is the same size class as the siblings in the rows.

ALPHA.seen: Clean alpha around the object. The mud strip and waterline are the exception the card allows, and no other backdrop or cast shadow is present.

OURS.seen: Shares the family's layout and mud base, with no sign of donor or vanilla art.

OWNER_NOTES.seen: No bright red, no yellow/black striping tape. Plain treated timber and galvanized steel read as a present-day structure, and Industrial is now the ugly cement barrier he asked for.

LEGIBLE.seen: At the smallest row it still reads as a dark post-and-board barrier with pale caps, distinct from the siblings, though board detail is lost.

findings.seen: The dark brown boards sit close in value to the brown ground and mud, so the panels merge at the smallest scale and mostly the caps and collars carry the read.
findings.quote: does not read at 32 px/cell (advisory by the brief)
findings.fix: The timber boards carry slightly lighter top edges and stronger gaps between boards, so the panels separate from brown ground at 32 px per cell.

findings.seen: The barrier runs along a strong diagonal, closer to an isometric construction than an on-axis 35-degree building view. All the sibling looks share this and the owner approved the family, so it is not specific to this look.
findings.fix: The barrier keeps the family's existing construction, with the top faces of caps and boards lit and visible.

reply.subject: RM_SiltTrap_Modern
reply.image_seen: 1: enlarged timber baffle with steel fittings; 2: isolated south sprite; 3: baffle beside a human; 4: three reference siblings; 5–7: four-look comparison rows at decreasing scales.

concerns.evidence: In south.png, the square post caps show visible top surfaces above shaded front and side bands, the posts remain vertical and parallel, and the boards recede consistently along the barrier. These support an elevated orthographic view; the diagonal barrier orientation does not itself indicate a wrong camera. The sibling and comparison panels show the same coherent perspective.
